doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: Joe Venuti pranks and the Whiteman 50th Anniversary album
summary: Willcox repeats that Venuti got him back playing; Gallodoro tells of Venuti's prank of summoning bass players and discusses the 50th Anniversary Rhapsody in Blue recording.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Buddy Tate, Milt Hinton. Marvelous guys. I’m talking about, oh, twenty years ago. Remember when I told you Joe Venuti asked me to come with him?
And that is what did it. It brought me right out of the woods fast.
Excuse me for laughing. You know the story that Joe Venuti was a prankster. He calls I think six bass players, I think string bass players or tuba, I never got that straight.
I think it was tuba, from what I’ve read.
“Meet me on 5th Avenue and 55th” or whatever, then he calls another one. He calls about five or six bass players to meet at the same time.
He told them it was a gig or something?

Yeah. He was a great violinist. Incidentally on the “50th Anniversary” album that I did the “Rhapsody in Blue,” and unabridged we do the whole thing with Buddy Reid. Tommy Dorsey is on this, Jimmy Dorsey is on it, a lot of guys.
Exactly. The sound is great. I was about to say something about that. It skipped my mind just for the moment.
